answer: Neighborhood Persistence Weighting. Each agent's influence is scaled by the number of distinct counterparties that keep transacting with it across rolling epochs, so a cluster of fresh identities that only trade among themselves forms an isolated island with near-zero external weight. A real participant's transaction ripple must reach established, unrelated nodes to count. An attacker must sustain organic-looking trade with many independent agents over several epochs, paying real fees and inventory costs per identity while each new node stays a frozen glacier of no influence until bridged.
